newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE BUSINESS OPTIMISM LOOKING UP.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE BUSINESS OPTIMISM LOOKING UP.

text.p: Singapore said on Tuesday that businesses in the manufacturing and financial sectors were generally optimistic for the second half of this year.
But the extent of optimism varied from industry to industry, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said in a statement.
Industrialists were cautiously optimistic about the general business climate with a net weighted balance of 17 percent of them foreseeing an improved business outlook, the statement said.
Expectations in the commerce, transport and storage sectors had turned more favourable, and the manufacturing sector expected to recover in the second half, it said.

Commerce and hub services were also likely to benefit from the recovery of the electronics sector and stronger trade growth, while mobile communications and construction should continue to sustain strong growth in the second half, the statement said.

The Ministry said that, taking all these factors into consideration, it was revising its forecast for Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the year to six to seven percent from five to seven percent previously.
Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong had announced the GDP forecast revision on Friday.
